quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It improves driving skills but harms judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It does not affect driving skills or judgment.
It does not affect judgment but harms driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and makes it hard to see clearly. It also makes it difficult to judge speed and distance. Alcohol lowers your caution and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, you should turn into:

options.text: The lane closest to the lane you were just in.
The lane marked with an arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the lane you were just in.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane next to your previous lane. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: To turn left from a multi-lane, one-way street or highway, start from:
questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multi-lane streets and highways.

questions.question: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at:
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are white lines across traffic lanes at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where to stop.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, slow down and yield to:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and all vehicles already in the roundabout before you enter.

questions.question: Driving faster affects your field of vision by:

options.text: Making it easier to see cross traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making it narrower.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your field of vision becomes smaller. You must pay extra attention to hazards when driving at higher speeds.

questions.question: You should be careful when passing large vehicles and avoid driving beside them for long periods of time.
questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have large blind spots on both sides. Either drop back or move ahead when driving next to a large vehicle to stay safe.

questions.question: If a traffic light is out due to a power outage, you should:

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Turn on hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat it like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: Treat a broken traffic light like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers as needed, then proceed carefully through the intersection when it is your turn.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means:

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming next. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: This sign warns you of:

options.text: No turns allowed on this road.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Several curves ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of three or more curves in the road ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A lane is ending or the road is narrowing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane is ending or the road is narrowing ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns that the right lane is ending or the road is narrowing.

questions.question: A stop is required at an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings. Where should you stop?

options.text: You do not need to stop.
Slow down to make sure crossing traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see at least 200 feet on either side, even if you enter the intersecting roadway.
Stop where you can see approaching traffic clearly before entering the intersecting roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can see approaching traffic clearly before entering the intersecting roadway.
questions.explanation: Without a stop line or crosswalk, stop at the nearest point to the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic. Do not enter the intersecting roadway to get a better view.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road without bicycle lanes and a cyclist is ahead of you going the same direction. How should you pass safely?

options.text: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass while leaving enough space between you and the cyclist.
Keep driving straight. The cyclist must get out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk to let the cyclist know you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass while leaving enough space between you and the cyclist.
questions.explanation: Pass a cyclist the same way you pass any vehicle. Keep at least 3 feet of space on regular roads or 5 feet on faster roads or when passing multiple cyclists. Do not honk unless necessary—it may startle riders and cause a crash.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: You feel tired while driving. What should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop driving.
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence. Stop driving if you feel tired.

questions.question: A traffic light shows a green arrow and a red light. What does this mean?

options.text: You can only drive straight ahead.
You can only drive in the direction the green arrow points.
You must wait for a solid green light to go in any direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only drive in the direction the green arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction the arrow points, and only if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your ability to judge speed and distance is affected.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows reaction time, reduces vision, changes your judgment of speed and distance, reduces your ability to recover from headlight glare, and often reduces your care about taking risks.

questions.question: When turning left, you have the right-of-way at which traffic signal?
questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A green arrow pointing left gives you the right-of-way. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean?

options.text: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
You do not have to stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign do?

options.text: Warns of existing or possible hazards.
Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.
Alerts drivers to food and gas locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns of existing or possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of hazards ahead. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: When can you carefully go through a yellow light?

options.text: An emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when a yellow light appears, you may carefully continue through it.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: You must stop immediately and back up.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and warn you that construction or maintenance work is happening on or near the road. Drive with extra care when you see these signs.

questions.question: How can you reduce the chance of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep tires filled to the correct air pressure.
Replace tires that are worn or bald.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your vehicle slides on water between the tires and the road. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase hydroplaning risk.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. What should you do?

options.text: Signal when it is safe for them to pass.
Look for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane when another driver passes you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and reduce your speed so the passing vehicle can return to the right lane easily.

questions.question: What do orange signs indicate?
questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone signs.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers that workers are on or near the highway.
